rules.rationale: This unconditional equation defines the fresh domain predicate definedProjectStr in terms of K's generated Str sort predicate.

This simplification characterizes the definedness of the pre-existing partial Val-to-Str cast; it is an additional trusted sort-domain fact and is not separately proved with this exact statement by prove.sh.
This guarded equation is a defining clause for the fresh named proof term projectStrTotal on the domain where the partial Str projection is defined.
This reverse normalization equation is part of the equational definition of projectStrTotal, orienting a defined partial cast to the fresh named proof term.
This equation defines total projection on an input already statically known to be a Str by returning that input unchanged.
Projector idempotence is an extra reusable simplification fact beyond the base projector clauses, and Stage 1 does not first prove this exact rule in a module that omits it.
This destructor equation defines codesOf for the sole modeled string constructor by returning its IntSeq payload.
This is the empty-sequence base equation of the recursively defined allStrings input-domain predicate.
This is the cons recurrence defining allStrings by checking the head's string domain, excluding references, and recurring on the tail.

This simplification extends the fixed set(str) observation to a guarded dynamic Val through projection. Stage 1 proves only the different static constructor equation, so this exact dynamic rule remains a trusted domain lemma.
This simplification extends fixed string less-than to guarded dynamic Val operands. The separate Stage 1 claim has static str constructors and therefore does not prove this exact rule.
This equation defines the uniqueCount mathematical summary as the length of the supplied distinct-code computation.
This equation defines the candidateWins comparator summary from score ordering and lexicographic tie-breaking.
This is the empty-sequence base equation of the bestWord fold.
This structurally decreasing cons recurrence defines bestWord by retaining or replacing the accumulator according to candidateWins.
This is the empty-sequence base equation of the bestScore fold.
This structurally decreasing cons recurrence defines bestScore in lockstep with the bestWord choice.
This is the empty-sequence base equation defining the final loop-target summary lastWord.
This structurally decreasing recurrence defines lastWord as the final element encountered, or the incoming accumulator when no element remains.
This is the empty-sequence base equation defining the final temporary-score summary lastScore.
This structurally decreasing recurrence defines lastScore as the uniqueCount of the final encountered element.
